Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

proud adjective

pleased with what one has or has done

also proud of, be proud of, take pride in, pride, I’m proud of you

classical

Cic. Att. 1.16.8: nōn enim mihi videor īnsolenter glōriārī
Traupman 156: glōrior (+ abl., dē or in), to be proud of

glōrior, glōriārī, glōriātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent: with the ablative, with dē or in and the ablative, or with an accusative and infinitive

be proud of, pride oneself on; boast

Pride that speaks: to glory in something, and so often to boast (Lewis & Short). For a parent’s quiet pride in a child, Latin says the joy instead: gaudeō, laetor (see glad).

Other words

  • superbus, superba, superbum — proud (of), with the ablative

    adjective: with the ablative of the cause · also used · classical · Mart. 10.37.17–19: vēnātor captā maele superbus adest

    (in hōc sēnsū vōx poētica et post Augustum: Verg., Mart., Sen.)

    In classical prose superbus is haughty, arrogant (see proud, arrogant); the good sense, proud of something, splendid, is poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

  • glōria, glōriae f. — pride, source of pride; glory

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.1.4: glōriae quidem videō fore; Traupman 156: glōria, pride, source of pride

    “It is something to be proud of”: glōriae est, with the double dative.

Examples

  • idem ego ille (nōn enim mihi videor īnsolenter glōriārī cum dē mē apud tē loquor, in eā praesertim epistulā quam nōlō aliīs legī) idem inquam ego recreāvī adflīctōs animōs bonōrum

    it was I, the same man (for I don’t think I’m being immodestly proud when I speak of myself to you, especially in a letter I don’t want others to read), I say, who revived the spirits of the loyal menCic. Att. 1.16.8

  • Vah, glōriāre ēvēnisse ex sententiā?

    What, are you proud that it turned out as you wanted?Ter. Haut. 765

  • dum loquor, ecce redit sportā piscātor inānī, vēnātor captā maele superbus adest: omnis ab urbānō venit ad mare cēna macellō

    as I speak, look, the fisherman comes back with an empty basket, the hunter arrives proud of the badger he caught: the whole dinner by the sea comes from the town marketMart. 10.37.17–19

See also proud, glad, praise.

SourcesLewis & Short: glorior · Lewis & Short: superbus · Lewis & Short: gloria
